label: ℓ(ℓ+1) is one object seen six times, not six findings

label: √6 at f is untestable: L = −∞ at every f opening

label: Q.final's hydrogenic zero is algebraic, not a prediction
quote: **Q.final's hydrogenic zero is algebraic, not a prediction.** At Nₑ = 1 the factor (Nₑ−1)/Nₑ vanishes, so δ = 0 identically for every charge and every C(Z). No parameter can move it. That makes "hydrogenic output EXACTLY zero" a tautology of the form rather than something 110 rows confirm.

label: The refuted family is Nilsson's modified oscillator; kappa and mu were never universal
quote: **The refuted family is Nilsson's modified oscillator.** H = HO − 2κℏω₀[l·s − μ(l² − ⟨l²⟩_N)] ... register 1368 never named it. ... The literature says the parameters were **never claimed to be universal** ... κ_n = 0.0588, μ_n = 0.328 for the actinide region against κ = 0.0601, μ = 0.448 for light nuclei ... the failure is *exact and structural*

label: Janet's E = 0 is forced, not earned

The limit was my data's edge, not the subject's.

I flagged at the time that I *expected* about 82 and got 28 — which meant my step extractor was itself broken ... **So the 28 is a bad null and should be recomputed**, not carried.

label: The eight recorded a-values are reconstructions, not measurements

So they are **reconstructions from prior runs, not measurements**, and 1403 and 1409 are claiming agreement with a previously computed trajectory. That is weaker than it reads, and worth annotating.

label: Monotone-chain filter asserted, not computed, for Lambda-traj

For Λ_traj's six I asserted each was a chain because each was an ordered count, and did not run the step test. That is very likely why you get seven closures and I got three ... **Trust your seven over my three.**

label: Madelung null corrected from 28 to 96
quote: **The null was not 28. It is 96.** Plain Madelung, scored on the same 106 clean steps the corridor uses, given the observed configuration at Z−1: **96 of 106, ninety-one percent.** Free-running, generating its own configurations from hydrogen: 94. label: Observation ends at Z=102, not 108; four edges
quote: **So I had the edge in the wrong place, and it's worth correcting plainly.** I told you 108 was where spectroscopically determined ground configurations end. It isn't. **Observation ends at 102.** What NIST lists for 103 through 108 are configurations from calculation and chemical homology — and the fetch itself showed it: every ionisation energy in those five rows carried a flag
why: It fixes the denominator of every score in the project and adds a third and fourth 'edge' (record vs observation) that registers 1395 and 1426 collapsed in opposite directions.

label: Scorer was fitted; 99 in sample, 90 held out
quote: Placing a from step Z's own corridor uses `brack.py`'s corridor, which was built *from the observed entrant at Z*. So the answer sets the parameter that produces the answer. Held out properly — a placed only from corridors already revealed at earlier steps, then the step predicted, then the step revealed — IN-SAMPLE 99 of 106 OUT-OF-SAMPLE 90 of 106
why: The project's most-quoted figure (99 of 106) is a fitting result, not a generation result; a future worker quoting it without the held-out 90 repeats the exact error.

label: delta = a√p is impossible, not merely wrong
quote: **The WKB route is closed, and it closes harder than I expected. δ = a√p is not merely wrong — it is impossible.** **Structurally.** In quantum defect theory δ is *bounded* as n → ∞; that boundedness is what makes a Rydberg series converge to the ionisation limit ... Our a√(n−ℓ−1) **diverges**. A bounded quantity and a divergent one cannot be equal, and no refitting of a repairs that.
why: It closes queue item A5b permanently and corrects 1416, which had called the failure the operator's rather than the relation's.

label: Atomic table is not additively representable as one system
quote: I wrote in 1461 that the atomic order *is* additively representable because 106 of 106 corridors are non-empty. Applying that entry's own imported warning to that entry: **it isn't.** ν has one parameter, so those are **106 separate one-dimensional feasibility results, not one system.** Solved as one system the table is **infeasible** — the running intersection empties fourteen times.
why: '106 of 106' is quoted throughout as a table-level result when it is a per-element one; the distinction decides what the corridor result actually claims.

label: The 94 reproduces none of the eight recorded a values
quote: **The rule reproduces none of the eight recorded a values.** Zero of eight. Its trajectory takes five distinct values, moves ten times, and only one of those values is a corridor endpoint at all. Its dominant value, 0.9828, is √(1/√2 × 1/(√3−1)) — a geometric mean of two crossings from *adjacent* groups, which is **not among the nineteen surds**. ... **The score does not identify the trajectory.**
why: Without this qualification beside it the 94 reads as a confirmation of the recorded walk, and the exception-recovery would be misattributed to a placement rather than to the form.

label: Shared trajectory origin at a=1.000 was a hard-coded default

I wrote that as a finding twenty minutes after setting the default myself.
why: A registered finding is withdrawn here; the true replacement — that the walk's origin is free because lithium's corridor is (0, ∞) — is register 1414's first instance.

label: Register 1493's Farkas cancellation reading is wrong

Δ(NEC≥2) and Δ(NEC≥3) correlation +0.905 SAME sign 86.5% OPPOSITE signs 0.9% (20 of 2,210) **It is not a cancellation.** ... register 1493's reading of the +16/−9 as an infeasibility signature is wrong. ... So the eight attacks weren't weak. They were **aimed along the grain**.

quote: I supplied 0092640X86900158 → Ivanova et al., pp. 419–428 correct 0092640X86900185 → Theodosiou et al., pp. 473–486 ... **58 for 85.** That's the worst shape a typo can take — it doesn't 404, it returns something plausible with the right journal, year and subject area. ... a false failure closes an avenue nobody ever tried.

quote: **PR3 — solved with U+2217 ∗, the ASTERISK OPERATOR.** ... 37 replaced (14 escaped, 23 raw) — 0 notation asterisks remain / unbalanced italics: 25 → 14 ... **the escape never worked.** Four of the six entries the queue called *"escaped correctly"* — 904, 943, 1275, 1302 — **still read as unbalanced** ... **PR5's audit 26 would have fired on correctly-escaped entries forever.**
why: Supersedes the queue's escape plan, and records that the previously-approved fix would have permanently broken the audit it was meant to enable.

label: E is identically zero at observability; register 1602 finding falls
quote: > **If an index admits exactly what can be observed, E is identically zero at observability. For every index. Always.** ... **And register 1602's finding falls with it.** I built the jK cell set *from* the triangle rule, then tested its defect cells *against* the triangle rule. Same set, asked twice. "All eight are triangle-rule violations" isn't a discovery.

label: The 600 unlockable cells withdrawn: rank is not reach
quote: **First fault: rank is not reach.** I called a cell unreachable when its rank exceeded the seed's 92. But **rank is a sum and reach is dominance in every coordinate.** ... Recomputed on dominance: **the count of bound-open cells with no witness above them is zero.** Not 600. ... **Second fault, and it's worse: all six hundred carry the bound *"derived by symmetry; no measurement required."***
why: Withdraws a headline claim from register 1610; without it the 600-cell 'cheapest move' stays on the board.

Then: require 6+ levels per group 0.619 a pure 1/n² Rydberg series 0.644 ← no chaos in it whatever **The statistic can't distinguish our data from textbook hydrogen** ... It measures the series law, not repulsion.

label: There is no fetch cache: only a permitted-URL set

There never was.** no permitted URL matches → REFUSED, and you know it a permitted URL matches → SERVED — the PERMITTED url, not the one asked for **Register 1595 said "one response per host and path per session."** That fits every observation and gets the cause wrong ... Register 1628 then compounded it by describing two mechanisms where there is one.

label: Charge axis is 1-based; no unbuilt charge-0 face
quote: R 1648 misread the charge axis: it is 1-based, charge = 1 *is* the neutral, which He I at (2,1) proves. There is no unbuilt charge-0 face; all 29 neutrals already had slots.

label: 306 of 554 staged rows are not series
quote: Both options assumed all 554 staged rows are series. **306 of them are not.** They span a single n, so their "members" are J-components of one level — Al I `4P n=3-3` has three members, all at n=3, spread 0.00762, graded **tier A**. That spread is fine-structure splitting, not series convergence.
why: Invalidates R 1649's tier census at 55% and shows the collision problem was never the real obstacle.

label: Al I nd labels are ordering labels, not quantum numbers
quote: **The Al I nd labels are ordering labels, not principal quantum numbers.** A quantum defect computed from them is not a physical quantity — which is why it rises monotonically instead of staying flat, and why any δ̄ for this channel depends entirely on which labelling convention was used.
identifiers: Al I; Appendix C δ̄; Martin & Zalubas
why: Separates monotonicity (a property of the ordering) from delta-bar (a property of the labelling), making r_l refusable rather than evaluable for such channels.

label: Coverage recomputed 685 to 497, then demoted to a floor
quote: **Coverage recomputed. 497 of 1,000, not 685.** [...] **The old 685 was inflated by 188 cells**, and the inflation was exactly the three tests going unapplied. Half the collection, not two-thirds. That number should replace the earlier one wherever it appears.
why: A superseded number explicitly ordered to be replaced wherever it appears; the later test-1 collapse then demotes 497 itself to a floor.

label: Lambda's stated caps do not reproduce 976 cells
quote: **ℓ ≤ 1, not ℓ ≤ 2.** §3.3's "caps (3,3,2,3)" does not reproduce 976 under §2.1's constraints; (3,3,1,3) with k ≥ 1 reproduces 976 and every other stated invariant. [...] **And k ≥ 1 is nowhere stated as a constraint** — §2.1 says "seven constraints, four origins, and nothing else," but the object needs an eighth condition

label: Duality convention resolved to sigma(x) = max minus x
quote: | σ | survivors | all even rank | signed sum | |---|---|---|---| | **max − x** | **8** | **yes** | **+8** | | max + min − x | 112 | no | 0 | The rank multiset of the eight is 6, 8², 10², 12², 14 — symmetric about 10, all even, signed contribution +8, against F(−1) = +2 for the whole object.
why: Fixes which of two duality conventions the book's stated count of 8 survivors depends on; the other gives 112 and 0.

label: Sign change is not the failure condition; test 1 deleted
quote: A sign change is not the failure condition. δ rising is. A + → − crossing is a fall and is harmless. A − → + crossing is a rise and inverts the order. ... So there is no test 1. It collapses into test 2 — δ strictly decreasing in ℓ — which subsumes it and is strictly narrower. I had been carrying an over-broad exclusion for four turns
why: Without this the framework retains a deleted, over-broad admissibility test and every coverage count computed under it is wrong.

label: Coverage figure bounded in (497, 685), three figures withdrawn
quote: That is three withdrawn coverage figures in a row — 685, then 497, now 497-as-floor — and every revision came from actually running the thing rather than from re-reading it. ... 685 excluded nothing correctly (channel mixing), 497 excluded too much (over-broad test 1), so the number lies in (497, 685)
why: Records that no point coverage value is defensible and why each superseded figure bounds the true one.

label: Law that an open index closes itself fails 4/7
quote: The chromosome index is the counterexample that decides it. E = 2.89 × 10⁹, the repair is a free relabelling, it has been available and unexecuted through two reference builds and seventeen years. **An index with three billion admitted-and-absent cells and a costless repair has not moved one step.** That is not something trying to close itself.
why: A proposed law tested and replaced, with two forward predictions attached that would falsify the replacement.

label: The 62,002 Mg perturber anchor was never independent
quote: **The 62,002 anchor was never independent.** For a p² configuration the three terms are −5F₂, +F₂, +10F₂ — pure angular integers on one radial scale. From the two *observed* terms: F₂ = 694.8 ... and first-order places ¹D at **62,022, or 351 cm⁻¹ above the limit**. The earlier session's "independently located at 62,002, 331 cm⁻¹ above the limit" is this arithmetic, not a measurement.
why: A number treated as an external constraint across two sessions is shown to be a first-order estimate; unrecorded, the circularity re-seeds.

label: 61,453 is a truncation, not an invariant of the lattice
quote: **61,453 is a property of a truncation, not an invariant of Λ₈**, and it shouldn't be quoted as one. Neither should anything derived from region fractions computed on it — the 32.23% inward, the 4.74% realisable, the 0.38% diagonal all move when the caps move. ... The inward region (e < n): e ≤ 5 → 63.48% ... e ≤ 62 → **3.42%**. It shrinks monotonically toward zero as the cap rises
why: Retires the framework's most-quoted number and every region fraction derived from it; leaving it unrecorded means those figures keep circulating as invariants.

label: §9.4 rejects sublattice-hood, not lattice-hood
quote: §9.4 ... is a *sufficient condition for sublattice-hood*. It has been used throughout the project as a rejection criterion: for the h axis, for metric coordinates in §22.2 with its 14,293 failures, for L, for spin projection, for Z. Every one of those rejections establishes "not a sublattice of the product." None of them establishes "not a lattice."
why: Every past rejection made on §9.4 grounds is re-opened; a future worker quoting those rejections as proofs of non-lattice-hood would be wrong.

label: d2 term ordering constraint withdraws the Ca 3d2 1D estimate
quote: For d², the term ordering isn't a convention — it's fixed by C/B, since ¹D < ³P exactly when C/B < 5. Ca's ³P sits at 48,550. The earlier estimate puts ¹D at 48,900, **349 cm⁻¹ above ³P**, which requires **C/B = 5.52**. The ratio method gives 47,876, implying C/B = 4.00, comfortably below. ... My Ca 3d² ¹D estimate of 48,800–49,000 ... appears to be wrong by about 1,000 cm⁻¹.
why: A cheap deductive constraint that caught an error three fitted analyses missed, and withdraws a number carried through many turns.

label: Ordinal claims could not have failed; the 123/124 tally deflated
quote: I twice predicted the ordering would break somewhere, and twice nothing broke. That wasn't luck: T is *exactly* monotone in Z_eff/ν, so no coordinate that moves Z_eff/ν in one direction can produce a violation. **The ordinal claims couldn't have failed, and the cardinal ones couldn't have succeeded in absolute form.** The 123/124 tally wasn't a discovery about the lattice
why: Withdraws the apparent 100% verification record as evidence for the framework and dissolves a 'boundary' reported several turns earlier.

label: Ninth axis 2J_core <= k admissible; Lambda-8 not maximal
quote: **Definition C — 2J_core ≤ k — is closed (zero join and meet failures across 1,400 sampled pairs of 367,833 cells) and admits a 9-box at (3,1,5,4,3,1,3,2,1). Order dimension 9.** So a ninth axis exists. Λ₈ is not maximal.
why: Overturns the headline maximality claim; without it a future worker restates a refuted theorem.

label: Zero-invention result was tautological; physical set not closed
quote: **The physical set is not closed, at any dimension.** Spin parity breaks it immediately: (1,1) and (2,0) are both physical in (k, 2S), their join (2,1) is not... **So "Λ₈ has zero invention" was tautological.** What we measured at 0% was a set defined by §9.4-form *chain* constraints — and such a set is closed by construction. Measuring its completion cost was measuring nothing.
why: A claim asserted at least four times as a substantive result is shown vacuous; anyone reusing it repeats the error.

label: Offset-coordinate lattice breaks closure; closure or faithfulness
quote: The offset-coordinate lattice **breaks closure**, and badly. 222,075 join failures out of 1,023,165 pairs on the exhaustive test... Isolated closure does not imply joint closure, and I asserted the composite result without ever building it. ... **You can have closure or faithfulness, not both**
why: Retracts the 100%-physical offset-coordinate result reported one message earlier and states the surviving trade-off, plus a general methodological rule.

label: Theorem 4.1 false for Lambda; replaced by unconditional theorem
quote: **The old Theorem 4.1 is false for Λ** — 148 counterexamples in 335 closure-preserving functions. It holds only for products of chains, and Λ isn't one. **The correct theorem needs no hypotheses at all:** > If *h* : *L* → ℤ has a closed graph, then *h* is monotone and the graph is order-isomorphic to *L*. Hence adjoining *h* never raises the order dimension.
why: Replaces the central order-theoretic theorem with a correct hypothesis-free version and records the counterexample count.

label: Conjecture 6.1 promoted to Theorem 6.1 with proof
quote: > **Theorem 6.1.** *No admissible coordinate system is order-isomorphic to the physical set.* > > *Proof.* An admissible family is closed under componentwise join and meet (Prop 2.1)... The physical set is not a lattice — at ℓ = 1 the pair (1,1), (2,0) has two incomparable minimal upper bounds, (2,2) and (3,1), so no least upper bound exists.
why: Removes the paper's only open conjecture by supplying its proof and the correct reason the chain counterexample fails.

label: Fine-structure coverage is 58.8%, and the mechanism is non-monotonicity
quote: **Question 2 — the 35.3% anomaly — is settled, and 35.3% does not reproduce.** Recomputing from the Ca II and Ba II fine-structure data gives **10/17 = 58.8%** ... These sequences are **monotone in neither direction**, which is a stronger and simpler disqualification than "too flat to bracket". ... Both accounts offered in §15.4 are wrong.
why: Corrects a published exclusion figure and replaces its stated mechanism with the right one.

label: Energy is anti-monotone in S; monotone in f only below defect collapse
quote: the correct statement is that energy is separately monotone in *n*, ℓ, *k*, *q*, *e* and *g*, **anti-monotone in *S***, and monotone in *f* only below the ℓ at which the defect vanishes. ... **Restricted to *f* ≤ 2 with the spin axis reversed: 83/83 = 100.0%.**
why: Falsifies the symmetric 'monotone in every coordinate' claim and explains why the derived ordinal coordinate carries minus signs.

label: Multi-subshell gap closed by summing coordinate G = g1+g2
quote: Conservation *g*₁ + *g*₂ ≤ *q* is a bound on a sum — so make the sum a coordinate. Replacing the transfer counts by (*g*₁, *G* = *g*₁+*g*₂) turns the constraints into *g*₁ ≤ *G* ≤ *q*, both of §9.4 form ... **1,040 cells, all 540,280 pairs, zero failures, and a 7-box.** ... The map is a bijection onto an admissible lattice but **not an order isomorphism**
why: Closes the coverage gap that no coordinate was thought to fix, and quantifies what Theorem 6.1 says it must cost.

label: H-invariance theorems cover meet and join but not comparability
quote: **Only meet, join and things built from them are *H*-invariant.** Comparability isn't. Neither is the order relation, nor up-set size — and comparability is what Part II actually uses. ... I reported a narrow theorem as a general one. ... A vacuous complement is what a mis-posed question looks like from the inside
why: Bounds the scope of the estimation theorems and records the diagnostic that a vacuous excluded class signals a mis-posed question.

label: Convergence model withdrawn: residual bounded by imagination
quote: **The model predicted 0.4 defects. I found four.** And the reason is instructive rather than embarrassing: **it assumed each pass samples the same population at the same rate.** It doesn't. ... **we cannot bound the residual, because the limiting quantity is not detection rate but imagination**, and a category never checked has unknown occupancy.
why: Withdraws a published error model and replaces it with the correct account of why audit yield does not decay to zero.

label: V closed form refutes the 17-49 operational floor
quote: **The closed form checks out.** *V* ≈ 4|*y*′|/(*h*|*y*″|) errs by 0.03–0.3% at *x* = 10 ... For a Rydberg channel *Z*, *R* and δ cancel identically, giving *V*(ν) = 4ν/3 + 4/(9ν), exact at 32/11 ... **Six single, resolved, Rule-1-compliant channels sit at 4.2–6.5**, which the paper claimed was impossible.
why: Turns three empirical numbers into one expression and overturns the paper's central practical claim about the cost of the bracket.

label: The 0.27% coverage figure used the wrong denominator
quote: **my own 0.27% figure was measuring the wrong thing.** ... **So expanding to all 198 Handbook spectra would add zero verified cells.** ... **That universe is of order 50–100 spectra, not 7,139.** Against that denominator the paper's 19 spectra and 24 channels is **20–40%**, not 0.27%.
why: Corrects the scope statistic by a factor of a hundred and defines the census that would let a completeness claim be defended.

Same lever, two ends: **E = 0 is strong exactly in proportion to the size of the ambient box it was computed in.** A zero must state both its fibration and its coordinate list or it states nothing.
why: Governs how every E=0 claim in the corpus must be read and stated; without it a zero can be manufactured by refining the fibration.

label: B.2.21 — the five conditions for a safe repair
quote: **B.2.21 — What a safe repair requires.** Five conditions: **(i)** the invariant written down before the edit; **(ii)** the invariant computable in §B.2.20's sense ... **(iii)** the edit a *permutation or insertion*, never a rewrite ... **(iv)** reversible, a copy taken first; **(v)** checked afterwards on source **and** artefact. Plus ... **prefer the smallest edit that removes the defect.**
why: The standing safety contract for every structural edit to the corpus, and the reason later permutations were judged cheap.

label: Audit 20 PROJECTION — a derived list that omits looks complete
quote: Every derived list is checked against an **independent enumeration of its source**, never against the rule that produced it. ... **a maintained list that omits a section is visibly short; a derived list that omits one looks complete.** The failure moved from forgetting to matching, and matching failures are silent.
identifiers: entry 294; entry 293; entry 216; B.2.17.13; audit 16 FIDELITY
why: Names the cost of every generate-instead-of-maintain repair and the standing check on it; correctness and completeness are different failures.

label: A check that carries a literal is narrowed to foreseen cases
quote: The pattern worth naming across 305 and 310: both times the audit that owned the defect had a *literal* in it — a hardcoded total, a fixed phrasing. **A check that carries a literal is a check that has been narrowed to the cases its author foresaw.** Audits 14 and 15 now both derive what they compare from the text instead.
identifiers: entry 305; entry 310; entry 318; audit 14 ARITHMETIC; audit 15 ENUMERATION; B.2.19.6
why: Explains three separate occasions when all twenty audits passed on a defective book, and the repair that applies to any future instrument.

label: §15.1.2 — the bracket is a deduction inward and a fit outward
quote: **So the rule your idea needs:** *presume the next bracket from the law that generates the widths, never from the pattern the widths make.* The first is deduction and survives; the second is extrapolation and is a fit however good it looks. ... **An index can say where something must have been between two observations and not where it will be after the last one**
why: States the boundary of the bracket with its measured demonstration (7 of 7 interior, 2.72% extrapolation error) and the rule that later defined the 9D/10D/11D relation.

label: Instrument takes its reference from the object, not the prose
quote: That's registers 305, 310 and now 337 — the same shape three times. **A literal inside an instrument narrows it to the cases foreseen when it was written**, and the rule is now stated plainly: *an instrument must take its reference from the object, never from the prose about the object.*
why: The general rule extracted from three repeated instrument failures; without it the next audit is written with the same class of defect.

label: A label is a name, not an address
quote: **A label is a name, not an address.** Entry 354 states it beside register 351's converse: an instrument must not name a thing by a label the book can change, and an author must not compute a label by hand.
why: The standing rule governing every renumbering, derived from repeated collisions; loses its paired converse if unrecorded.

label: Cap convention: unmarked figures are at (3, 3, 1, 3, 1)
quote: **84 paragraphs carry a cap-dependent figure. 69 of them name no cap — 82% relying on a rule that was not written down.** … **Now stated at §7.4:** every cap-dependent figure is at **(3, 3, 1, 3, 1)** unless the section names others … > **A cap-dependent figure without a stated cap is not thereby unqualified — it is at these caps.**
why: A convention in force from the first page and never written down; without it 69 paragraphs of figures have no stated frame.

label: Prime zeno update: work order as a closure operator
quote: Prime zeno directive update - Prioritize all work in order of fetch/search - read/encode - analysis/computation - interpretation/conclusion/report. - always finish/close each step/work before moving/continuing on to the next. (it isn't a pipeline — it's a closure operator … a reopen is legitimate only when a recorded fact triggered it.)
why: The author's own statement of the governing work discipline and the reason the reopen condition exists; the parenthetical is the load-bearing half.

label: A verification may never be cached across an edit
quote: And the check I ran to catch that **returned stale cached output.** Zeno skips a step that has already succeeded, so `fibre_check.py` handed back its pre-edit answer ... The harness needs a rule it does not have: **a verification must never be cached across an edit to the thing it verifies.**
why: Without it the zeno harness will silently re-report pre-edit results and conceal broken edits again.

label: §2.22 — corroboration must reference in both directions
quote: > **Any register entry that a proof, theorem, equation or expression settles must name that object, and the object must name the entry. A reference in one direction is a citation; a reference in both is an index.** ... **107 entries are corroborable and not searchable from what corroborates them.** ... **of 132 mathematical objects, four cite a register entry.**
why: A new protocol plus the measurement that forced it and the recovered bound repair ≤ φ(corroboration).

label: Never one heuristic — report the spread
quote: # §2.24 — Never one heuristic > **Where a quantity is reached by a heuristic rather than computed, run at least two heuristics of different kind and report the SPREAD. A single heuristic cannot tell you whether it is in the case where it works.**
why: Without it the twelve-cycle single-heuristic failure that invalidated five registers has no governing rule to prevent recurrence.

label: A source has an index, rarely the one with a search box
quote: > **A source has an index, and it is rarely the one with a search box.** **Three of four searches moved by changing the index rather than the query.** The ASD by spectrum against its compilations by element. *Seed* against **minimum cardinality generator** ... And poset complexity against **0-1 matrix recognition**
why: It is the retrieval method that opened three of four documents §19.5 recorded as closed, and it governs every future search.

label: Run the cheapest language combination; costs ranked by measurement
quote: **failed edits** — an anchor that misses costs a whole cycle. Assert the count first; split independent edits so one failure cannot lose the other. **This was the largest single drain today.** **text into context** — reading a file to find a line costs what the file costs. Grep and extract. **loops over arrays** ... **serial lookups** ... **echoing output** — present the file.
why: A user-instructed standing rule with a measured cost ordering that governs how all later sessions spend their budget.

label: A test's failure mode must be exhibited before it is trusted
quote: **Register 613: the probe I built to catch that could not fail.** `expected()` was a line-for-line copy of the criterion. ... A criterion cannot be checked by restating it. **What can be checked without restating it is monotonicity and exhaustiveness** ... > **A test whose failure mode has been exhibited is worth more than one that has only ever passed.**
why: States the repair method for tautological audits and the standard any new instrument must meet.

label: A generated document can lose its source entirely
quote: > **A generated document cannot drift from its source. It can lose one entirely — and only a check comparing the document to its own claims sees that.** ... `register_gen.py` read **chapter 28** — which the reconstruction thinned ... **so the complete record collapsed to the selection.** Recovered to `REGISTER-DATA.md`: **457 entries, 165–653.**
why: Two generators silently emptied when their source moved; the rule and both instances are the guard against a third.

label: Register 697 — reading degrades before writing does
quote: **Reading degrades before writing does.** > > Once a format is established and the source becomes hard to read, output continues at full fluency **from the pattern rather than the data**, and nothing internal marks the difference. > > **A truncated file announces itself. A confabulated one does not.** > > **So the rule is to stop at the first sign of strained reading, not at the first failure**
why: The stopping criterion derived from the fabrication; without it the rule reverts to 'stop at first failure', which the incident showed is too late.

label: Provenance filtering runs before J-consistency
quote: **Provenance filtering runs first.** A bracketed value isn't a weaker measurement — it's not a measurement. It can't participate in a test of measurement consistency.
why: Settles a filter-ordering question that would otherwise produce a circular agreement between a Ritz value and a measured one.

label: A joint fit whose answer moves across subsets reports perturbation
quote: **Ti III's seven series gave one limit at rms 0.0054. P I's eleven give three:** ns alone **84,811.8**, ns+np **84,883.7**, adding nd **84,714.5** — a spread of **170 cm⁻¹**, larger than any individual error bar. > **A fit whose answer moves when you drop a series is reporting the perturbation, not the limit.**
why: The precondition on the joint-fit move, and the reason P I was refused admission despite having its levels in hand.

label: Two bounds from the same relation are one statement twice
quote: > **Two bounds from the same relation are the same statement made twice.** **Which the compendium already knew.** `BRACKETED` has meant *"bounded above and below by different mechanisms"* since register 831. **`PROPAGATED` never carried the requirement.**
why: States the repair rule and shows the grading already forbade what the propagation was doing; the criterion now applies to every bounded cell.

label: Steps must be derived from measured cells only
quote: > **The walk manufactures pairs, and re-measuring on them finds structure it put there. 𝒮 must be derived from MEASURED cells only — never from walked ones — or the triple confirms itself.**
why: Names the exact circularity that makes the valuation closure confirm itself, with the numbers that expose it (iso at s tightening 1.13 to 1.08, steps 3 to 8).

label: Additive forms lose rank; multiplicative forms cannot hold exceptions
quote: > **The additive form fits values and destroys rank. The multiplicative form preserves rank and cannot fit values. That is exactly what your prime-factor intuition predicted: a product of positives cannot invert an order, and a sum of signed terms cannot help but.**
why: A general constraint on any equation meant to sit beside ordinal mechanisms, with the measured 102/205 against 205/205 that establishes it.

label: An index is its coordinates
quote: > **An index is its coordinates. Two objects with the same cells and different coordinates are different indices. E is a fact about each and never about the cells alone.** **Which means "the periodic table has E = 36" was never a complete sentence.**
why: Without it every recorded E in the compendium can be misread as intrinsic to a set of cells.

label: Compendia answer; the register argues
quote: **The four topical compendia answer and do not argue.** ... **And the Register *should* carry the arguments** ... **1216** — the point of order itself, recorded: **compendia answer, the register argues, and that is what keeps the book bounded.**
why: The document-architecture rule that keeps the book under 500 pages, and it names the exact front-matter violation it was applied to.

label: Lock independently measured quantities; refit one number at a time
quote: Agreed, and the rule should be explicit: **anything measured independently is locked, and only genuinely free numbers get fitted.** ... **Every previous refit moved three things at once and I couldn't tell which was real.** This one moves one number and the residuals are a diagnosis rather than noise.
why: Without it a future worker repeats the trap where an improved rms is bought by degrading a separately measured quantity.

label: No pooled fits across blocks; one coefficient per subshell
quote: **The index forbids this.** Λ_phys closed on (source, domain) with **no parameter of this work in the universal column** ... **A pooled fit across blocks is a claim of universality the index says cannot exist.** ... **The occupancy term is `b(n,ℓ)·q`, with one coefficient per subshell, measured within that subshell.** Not a function of n, not of ⟨r⟩, not of anything pooled.
why: A rule the human states was violated repeatedly, and the one msg 1902 asks be turned into a protocol; it governs every future fit.

label: The one microscope is ℛ; verification is a foundation not an endpoint
quote: **The single microscope is ℛ.** That's what the method actually is — every object becomes cells and coordinates, and then the same three questions apply: does it close, in which carrier, and what does the closure refuse.
why: States the method's operative stance in one sentence and the three questions that follow from it.

label: No-fitted-parameter claim travels with the provenance table
quote: **And the standing instruction**: the no-fitted-parameter claim and the provenance table travel together, always.
why: A standing publication rule guarding the solution's strongest claim from being quoted unsupported.

label: A generated artefact with a hand-edited region is not generated
quote: The general fault is worth keeping: an artefact called generated that has a hand-edited region is not generated, and REPRODUCTION checks the build runs, not that it round-trips.
why: States the defect class and the audit gap that let it through, applicable to every generated artefact in the work.

label: Never invent a cell or column; shuffle until it fits or one cell remains
quote: this is the error. We don't create or invent new information. We combine information about the same subject and let them work together force the solution. Instead of inventing a cell or column. Rearrange and shuffle the index until everything fits or 1 cell remains
why: A user ruling that governs every index construction and removed two spurious defect cells the moment it was applied.

label: Every generator diff-tested; in-place writers refuse partial output
quote: I've left it in the queue under I as the standing rule: *every generator is diff-tested, and any that writes in place must refuse partial output.* ... A generator that cannot produce its whole output must refuse to produce part of it.
why: Binds all future generators; explicitly left in the queue as prose rather than wired into the audit suite.

label: An axis is determined when its chain of values is monotone
quote: A note for construction. An axis is determined when a set/chain of values is monotonastic
why: The construction rule that immediately disqualified two of six proposed letters (c had zero envelope steps, Nₑ was Z renamed) and explained an inflated E.

label: NIST's blend column is a membership condition, not a quality flag
quote: Worth its own line somewhere: **NIST's blend column is not a data-quality annotation, it is a membership condition**, and results conditioned on it hold exactly when it separates — which is the separation hypothesis in a place it hadn't been applied.
why: The flag decided two independent results (twelve manufactured zeros in the L1M splitting, and 1391's Sc–Ti claim); treating it as advisory silently widens comparison sets until findings disappear.

label: 'Corrected at source' must be checked against the tree
quote: The record now carries that limitation explicitly, and a standing rule with it: **a register entry saying "corrected at source" is a claim about the tree and must be checked against the tree, not trusted.**
why: It names a class of loss PROVENANCE.md structurally cannot see — an edit lost inside a file that itself survived — and governs how every 'corrected at source' entry must be read.

label: Parse before writing; extract and parse every checkpoint
quote: The practice I should have had: **parse before writing, not after.** Both failures wrote a broken file and then discovered it. And checkpoints now get extracted and parsed rather than just created — which is how I know 1_9e is sound.
why: A declared governing practice for every future edit and checkpoint; without it the broken-checkpoint failure recurs.

label: R is complete on trees and incomplete on anything with a cycle
quote: **The same measure explains where the method works and predicts where it won't** — and it states the method's boundary: **ℛ is complete on trees and incomplete on anything carrying a cycle.** ... so every object the register has failed to close should be checked first for a cycle.
why: States the operator's domain of validity and prescribes a mechanical first check for every unclosed object.

label: A blank field is data; spot-checks must target the odd rows
quote: Two things I'd keep: **a spot-check that samples convenient rows can't see a fault in the odd ones** — it has to target the rows that *differ* from the rest. And **a blank field is data**; writing anything into it is fabrication however plausible the number's source.
why: Records the two rules learned from four fabricated theory values that passed their own spot-checks.

label: H3: five executable steps for populating an index by extraction
quote: 1 FIND THE SOURCE'S OWN FORMULA FOR ITS OWN GAPS ... 2 VALIDATE BEFORE USING ... 3 MEASURE THE SYSTEMATIC ERROR WHERE MEASUREMENT EXISTS ... 4 FIND THE MISSING DEPENDENCE ... 5 SEPARATE CONFIDENCE BY QUANTITY ... The prediction file says *PREDICTED, NOT MEASURED. NOT A CAPTURE.* in its first line.
why: A transferable five-step method plus the labelling rule and the ordering constraint that H1's re-coordinatisation must precede it.

label: List the whole tree before asking for anything
quote: The standing rule this adds, now on the board: **before asking for anything, list the whole tree.** A capture directory is a convention, not a boundary — and I mistook the convention for the fact, then asked you for what you'd already given twice over.
why: Names the exact failure mode (globbing one conventional directory) that cost three fetches for data already on disk.

label: Intake protocol: a conversation with a model is not a source
quote: **A conversation with a model isn't a source.** ... material sorts four ways: POINTER a paper, author, dataset → fetch from source CLAIM an assertion about physics or maths → board row, test stated before it runs FRAME a way of seeing the problem → usable immediately NUMBER any figure, coefficient, count → REFUSED until traced to a primary source
why: The written protocol governing all third-party model material, including the commitment that no input is summarised into an artefact and later cited as though the artefact established it.

label: Three shortcut retrieval routes convicted with causes
quote: 1. **Transcript recovery** — convicted: truncates bulk tables, invites completion-from-memory (Pb I), can't re-verify provenance 2. **Fetch from the queue file's URLs** — refused by the permission layer 3. **Search-then-fetch** — executes but substitutes: it serves whatever URL the search indexed, not the query I built.
why: A closed investigation of every cheap route with a verdict each; without it the same three shortcuts get retried and one silently substitutes atoms.

label: A narrowed search reports on what it admitted, not what was asked
quote: **The archives were never disjoint. My probe was.** ... I treated a listing as a population. ... *an instrument that narrows its own input reports on what it admitted, not on what it was asked about.* ... A negative result from a search is a statement about the search until the search's own scope has been audited.
why: A general rule about negative results, with the concrete instance (a directory counted as one listing entry) that produced a false 'completely disjoint' claim.

label: Corpus harness gate: nothing ships unless measured
quote: **nothing ships before the corpus harness passes, and MEASURE means measured.** The register stands at sixteen; the physics remains untouched at three audit generations deep.
why: A standing operational rule adopted mid-session and carried forward to every subsequent build; losing it loses the gate.

label: An audit must be shown capable of failing before it is trusted
quote: entry 318 adds the requirement mine had never met: *an audit must be shown capable of failing before it is trusted.* Applied immediately: I injected a single-digit fault into a companion document, and **the harness passed it** — my AGREEMENT probe tested presence, so a changed value simply vanished from the presence list.
why: Fault injection entered the standing operation only because the harness was convicted by it; without the record the rule reads as ceremony rather than a repaired defect.

label: Closure applied to non-monotone bounds is fabrication
quote: Applying ℛ to an unsorted index does not repair it — it *overwrites the bounds*. Toy case, computed: declared [10, 7, 13, 4] → after ℛ, [10, 10, 13, 13]. [...] Closure here is not repair. It is fabrication, in exactly P22's sense — and it arrives silently, with E = 0 as its certificate.
why: Names the one way E = 0 can be produced falsely and self-certified; the failure mode is indices that close wrongly and pass their own audit.

label: Only audits reading outside the work found real defects
quote: Every audit that reads the work found nothing wrong with the work. The three that found real defects — ATTRIBUTION, and PROJECTION twice — all read something outside it [...] **Six detector faults, three real defects, and every real one came from a comparison the work could not perform on itself.**
why: States what the twenty prime audits are actually good for, and why a self-referential audit set can pass a defective artefact.

label: Five requirements any ninth coordinate must satisfy
quote: A ninth coordinate h must satisfy five things: 1. **Integer-valued** ... 2. **§9.4 bound** — h ≤ φ(x) for a *single* existing coordinate x, with φ non-decreasing and a constant floor. 3. **Closure** ... 4. **Dimension** — adding h must produce a 9-box, or it isn't a new axis. 5. **Independence** — h must not be determined by the other eight, or Λ₉ is the graph of a function.
why: The explicit admissibility test for any proposed new axis; without it the h question is reopened from scratch each session.

label: Anchoring: withhold comparison values until the range is committed
quote: **The inputs support 23,984–24,386 (width 402). I reported 24,100–24,350 (width 250).** I narrowed the range by 38% without running any calculation that justified narrowing it. That's the anchoring. ... compute the prediction and its range *before* looking at any published estimate ... withhold the comparison value from me until the range is fixed
why: A demonstrated process failure and the one procedural fix that prevents it; it also invalidates any number produced under the same conditions.

label: Rule 1 corrected: same Rydberg sequence, defect-departure threshold
quote: > **Rule 1, corrected:** the cell must be interior on some axis **and belong to the same Rydberg sequence as its neighbours** — which the defect sequence itself tests. A member whose defect departs from its neighbours' by an order of magnitude more than they depart from each other is a collapsed or perturbed state and must be excluded.
why: An operational exclusion threshold with a numeric criterion the method depends on, stated nowhere else.

label: Rule 1 directional: extrapolation below forbidden, above permitted
quote: **Extrapolating below costs 446× on median; extrapolating above costs 0.28× — it is better than interpolation.** ... The rule should read: **extrapolation below the lowest measured member is forbidden; extrapolation above the highest is permitted under the same σ.** ... The old blanket 3.7× is documented as non-reproducible and unstable, since it inverts to 0.5× on removing two cells.
why: Rewrites one of the method's four rules and exposes the old cost figure as unstable; a future worker would otherwise forbid a permitted operation.

label: Rule 1 also requires a shared term set across the channel
quote: **Rule 1 now requires a shared term set, not just a shared channel.** Every earlier species satisfied this without being asked — alkaline earths and alkali-likes have complete listings at every *n* — so it never bound. It binds the moment the method meets an open-shell system.
why: A precondition discovered only on Sc II; without it a centroid mismatch reads as a failure of the observable.

label: Basic principles governing all later work
quote: - A complete index will always be self referencing. - A complete index will always be self defending. - Always audit results. - Always compute the results before assuming the results. - When a question is confusing, reframe the question. - All questions must close.
why: The declared governing principles, invoked by name in every later item and ultimately formalised as the completeness law.

label: Coherence bar forbidding caveat, gap, question, contradiction, assertion
quote: - a claim of true, total, and complete coherence cannot be made any of the following are present: caveat, gap, question, contradiction, assurtion.
why: The acceptance bar that decides the book's claim boundary and forced the elimination route over the derivation route.

label: Treat bounds and limits as coordinates; the path goes through them
quote: - treat bounds, constraint, and limits as coordinate values in a multilattice index. Let the index show you the answers and the path to them.
why: The declared principle that produced the bound-lattice, the three-axis classifier and the reading of failures as coordinates; later extended to "the path is always through the bounds, constraints, and limits".

label: Series-formula cells are consistency checks, not independent tests
quote: > **Cells resting on bracketed ASD values are consistency checks, not independent tests.** **For Al I that is 7 of 11 *n*s cells and 2 of 5 *n*f cells.** ... **This needs auditing across all 763 cells before the book states the figure**, and it will reduce the count of *independent* tests.
why: Governs how every cell count may be reported; a standing audit obligation raised by a cross-check.

label: Rule 1 is about direction, on whichever axis carries the defect
quote: > **Rule 1 is a rule about direction, and it holds on whichever axis carries the defect.** | ***n***, within a series | **446×** | 1× | **0.28×** | | ***Z***, along a sequence | **17.3%** | 1.3% | **2.1%** | **Same sign, same asymmetry, same cause** — δ varies fastest where the electron is loosely bound and flattens where it is tightly bound.
why: Generalises a series heuristic into a statement about defect stiffness on any axis, with both cost tables.

label: Rule 4a: constant-defect form inadmissible on a decreasing channel
quote: > **The constant-defect form may be used only if the constant does not exceed the last measured defect in the direction of extrapolation.** On a decreasing channel, δ̄ ≤ δ(last measured). And §13.2 explains why in the sharpest terms available: > **A rule that produces an estimate its own bracket excludes is not a rule about uncertainty. It is an error.**
why: A new clause to the method's rules, created because the book's only forecast violated it.

label: General order-k admissibility rule for finite differences
quote: > ***k* is admissible only while \|Δ^*k*T\| > 5·2^*k*·σ.** **That is computable per cell, it explains every anomaly above**, and it converts the purity index from a broken measure into one with a stated domain — **exactly the way ν_V rescued *V* in §14.9.**
why: One rule generalising the book's two separate admissibility criteria (r and nu_V), which the book states as two instances and never as the rule.

label: Apply P8 to every failure: the register is a list of bounds
quote: **The procedure** — three things per failure: what was attempted, what it excludes, which kind (upper · lower · negative · structural). **Then read the collection**... > **A register of withdrawals is a list of bounds. Read it that way and it stops being a confession.** ... > **Ten failures produced one exact statement. None of them was wasted, and none would have been kept without the protocol.**
why: A retained working protocol that turns the withdrawal register from a confession into an instrument, with its worked case and taxonomy.

label: Six prime audits, ordered by what a failure costs
quote: > **The first two can make the book WRONG. The next two can make it UNREADABLE AS AN ARGUMENT. The last two can make it UNUSABLE AS AN OBJECT.** **1 — LATTICE.** ... **2 — EQUATIONS.** ... **3 — CONSISTENCY.** ... **4 — REDUNDANCY.** *because a stale claim is a false claim that passed every other check.* **5 — ARTEFACT.** *because the source can be perfect and the page still wrong.* **6 — ...
why: The final ordering and the one-line justification for each audit's rank is the governing protocol for every later verification pass.

label: Ask the register, not the build, before a row goes to M
quote: **That is the third fault of the same kind in one session** — Λ_ladder, flag 5's owner, flag 4's fix. Each was a status read off a stale generated artefact and handed to you as a question you had already answered or the machinery already handled. The rule it earns: *before a row goes to M, ask the register, not the build.* That belongs in the register as a practice clause, not in a summary.
why: A practice clause explicitly earmarked for the register but recorded only in this chat, with the three failures that earned it.

label: Retrieval-only layer: closure confirmable, openness never
quote: **a chat without the bank can confirm a closure decisively and can never establish openness.**... Under R 1672 I can never audit a retrieval search's scope, so a negative from it stays a statement about the search. But a *positive* — finding the closure entry — is decisive.
why: Governs how any non-bank chat may report to the register; a false-negative fault class the board had already hit three times.

label: Enumerate before searching should read search before deriving
quote: The mechanism is the one §E.7 already named after nine instances: *enumerate before searching* should read **search before deriving**, and I ran four turns of derivation before one search. The search took one query. The correct order would have cost a minute and saved the run
why: A proposed amendment to a named standing rule, triggered by its tenth instance; unrecorded the rule keeps its weaker wording.

label: No claim may rest on a profile count
quote: **What did not survive is the cardinality.** 66 → 123 → 246 profiles, same physics, three carvings. The size of the index is not an invariant; it's an artefact of how finely you cut the coordinates. So no claim in this thread should ever rest on a profile count.
why: A governing prohibition on a class of quantity the reports repeatedly produce, established by a triple recarving with no change in content.

label: Prime zeno directive update: four strictly ordered phases
quote: Prime zeno directive update - Prioritize all work in order of fetch/search - read/encode - analysis/computation - interpretation/conclusion/report. - always finish/close each step/work before moving/continuing on to the next.
why: A standing operating directive issued to govern all subsequent work, stated only in conversation.

label: Hard closure with a repair gate at every phase boundary
quote: Rule logged: hard closure, with a **repair gate at every phase boundary** — a phase doesn't close until its known defects are fixed. ... when phase N+1 finds a defect *in phase N's output*, hard closure says phase N stays shut, so the fix lands at the close of N+1 — the phase where it was found.
why: The governing rule for how defects found downstream are discharged, chosen over both hard closure and reopen-on-trigger.

label: Operator clause: grade capped by measured reliability in the claim's domain
quote: **Operator clause.** *An entry's grade is the minimum of its source grade and the operator's measured reliability in the domain of the claim. Reliability is measured, never assumed, by committed predictions scored against retrieval. An unmeasured domain carries the lowest grade held in any measured domain, not the highest.*
why: Extends the Admission Law to the operator, and fixes that an unmeasured domain inherits the worst measured grade rather than the best.

label: Collision routes, never gates: contradiction raises priority
quote: **Admission Law, revised.** *An open index reads all outside content and admits it graded. Verification against the index's internal mathematics determines routing, not admission ... content contradicting the index is admitted at source grade and flagged as a collision. A collision is discharged only by re-deriving the internal result, never by refusing the content.*
why: The final form of the admission law, and the reason a gate would close the index against exactly the information that corrects it.

label: A biconditional licenses a merge only at every rung
quote: **Five merges, none that survives grading.** The rule tightens from "only biconditionals survive" to: **a biconditional licenses a merge only if it holds at every rung of the graded axis.** Merging on a fact true at one point and then grading the axis is the error, and I made it while explicitly checking for biconditionals.
identifiers: D ≡ N; L → S; SD → S; Sig; DN → S_corr
why: A rule with five data points behind it that governs every future coordinate consolidation; four merges failed for want of it.

label: A derived coordinate can never repair closure
quote: **A derived coordinate cannot repair closure.** RR reconstructs from cells alone — "No outside knowledge enters. ℛ(X) is what a reader could reconstruct from the cells alone" — and a reader given the cells cannot see that P was *defined* as a max over three others. ... **B.2.15 — what this failure excludes:** the entire class of derived-coordinate repairs, for every index, not just this one.
why: Excludes an entire class of repair attempts for every index, and explains why adding an axis strictly increases E.

label: Merging independent axes inflates envelopes; both repair directions fail
quote: **Any operation that reduces the coordinate count while preserving information moves constraints onto coarser axes**, and ℛ's envelopes get worse, not better, as an axis carries more distinctions. That is the mirror of the derived-coordinate result: adding a dependent axis inflates the box, and merging independent axes inflates the envelopes. **Both directions fail, for opposite reasons.**
why: Closes the second half of the repair search space with a stated mechanism, preventing repeat attempts at linearisation.

label: E's density asymmetry: E=0 informative at any density
quote: My density rule is **asymmetric and I stated it symmetrically.** Λ₁₃ sits at 0.42% — below my proposed threshold — yet **E = 0 there** ... > **E = 0 is informative at any density. E > 0 at low density measures sparsity rather than structure.**
why: A stated constraint on when E may be read at all, in its corrected asymmetric form — quoting the symmetric version would misgrade every low-density result.

label: Not every vocabulary is an index; E needs graded, related terms
quote: > **Not every vocabulary is an index.** V3, V5 and V6 have internal structure and close. V2 has none, and the operator cannot be applied to it meaningfully. ... **E is defined only where the terms are graded and related.** Given a bag of unrelated categorical scope conditions, the operator returns a number that depends on how you sorted the bag.
why: A stated limit on where the operator may be applied at all, discovered by a case where E depended on an arbitrary categorical ordering.
